The Business Analyst will act as the critical link between the Corporate Banking business (Liquidity & Cash Management) and Technology/Operations teams, translating business needs into clear functional requirements. The role supports the design, delivery, and continuous improvement of cash management products — including domestic and cross-border payments, liquidity structures (pooling, sweeping, notional pooling), virtual accounts, and digital banking channels — ensuring solutions meet client needs, regulatory requirements (SAMA), and internal risk/control standards.

  • Produce Business Requirement Documents (BRDs), Functional Specification Documents (FSDs), process flow diagrams, and user stories for change initiatives and new product launches.
  • Support end-to-end delivery of cash management initiatives including cash pooling, sweeping/topping arrangements, notional pooling, and multi-currency account structures.
  • Conduct gap analysis between current and target operating models, identifying process inefficiencies and automation opportunities.
  • Collaborate with Product Managers to support the design and rollout of new liquidity management solutions aligned with client and market demands.
  • Work closely with Compliance and Risk teams to ensure new products/features comply with SAMA regulations and internal governance frameworks.
  • Coordinate and support User Acceptance Testing (UAT), including test case preparation, defect tracking, and sign-off coordination.
  • Analyze transaction and liquidity data to identify trends, client behavior, and areas for product enhancement.
  • Support RFP responses, client onboarding requirements, and due diligence documentation for corporate clients using liquidity/cash management services.
  • Prepare MI reports, dashboards, and presentations for senior management on project status, product performance, and client usage.
  • Maintain up-to-date process documentation and ensure knowledge transfer to Operations and support teams.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Business Administration, Economics, Information Systems, or a related field.
  • Professional certification such as CBAP, CCM (Certified Cash Manager), or CTP (Certified Treasury Professional) is an advantage.

Experience

  • Minimum 3–7 years of experience as a Business Analyst within Corporate/Transaction/Wholesale Banking, with specific exposure to Cash Management and/or Liquidity Management products.
  • Proven experience working on cash management platforms (e.g., host-to-host connectivity, SWIFT, API banking, virtual accounts, liquidity structures).

  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills — able to bridge technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Fluency in English required; Arabic language proficiency strongly preferred given the local market focus.
  • High attention to detail with strong organizational and multitasking abilities.
  • Knowledge of SAMA regulations, AML/CFT requirements, and general banking compliance standards.

Key Performance Indicators (Typical)

  • Timely and accurate delivery of BRDs/FSDs for assigned initiatives.
  • Successful UAT completion rates and minimal post-go-live defects.
  • Stakeholder satisfaction scores (Business, IT, Operations).

Working Relationships

  • Internal: Corporate Banking Relationship Managers, Product Management, IT/Digital Delivery teams, Operations, Compliance & Risk, Finance.

Company Description

At CluePoints, we’re redefining how clinical trials are run. As the premier provider of Risk-Based Quality Management (RBQM) and Data Quality Oversight software, we harness advanced statistics, artificial intelligence, and machine learning to ensure the quality, accuracy, and integrity of clinical trial data, helping life sciences organizations bring safer, more effective treatments to patients faster.

We’re proud to be an ambitious, fast-growing technology scale-up with a dynamic and diverse international team representing more than 40 nationalities. Collaboration, flexibility, and continuous learning are part of our DNA.

At CluePoints, you’ll find a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and have fun along the way. Guided by our values of Care, Passion, and Smart Disruption, we’re united by a shared mission: to create smarter ways to run efficient clinical trials and deliver AI-powered insights that improve human outcomes worldwide.

We’re looking for anAI-First Software Engineer Engineerto help shape this next chapter.


The Role

As an AI-First Engineer, you will operate at the intersection of strong software engineering fundamentals and modern AI-assisted development. You will use state-of-the-art AI coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Codex-style agents) to generate and iterate on production-grade code — while applying human judgment, architectural thinking, and rigorous review to ensure quality, security, and compliance.

As part of our AI-First transformation, we are adopting Spec-Driven Development (SDD) across our engineering teams. Instead of moving straight from user stories into code, engineers write structured specifications that serve as the single source of truth for both human and AI-driven implementation. The spec is reviewed and approved before any code is written, and AI coding agents work within the constraints it defines.

Some of our squads are already working this way, and these roles will help scale the approach across the organisation. Experience with SDD frameworks such as OpenSpec, SpecKit, BMAD, or Superpowers is required.

This is not a traditional “ticket-driven” engineering role. Instead, you will:

  • Work in small, high-impact squads (4–5 people)
  • Operate within a Spec-Driven Development (SDD) framework
  • Treat AI as a powerful collaborator — not a replacement for engineering responsibility
  • Focus on integration, edge cases, system-level thinking, and production robustness
  • Your output will be amplified by AI — but your judgment will define its quality.

Responsibilities

AI-Assisted Implementation

  • Use AI coding tools to generate and iterate on implementation code
  • Rapidlyprototypemultiple technical approaches with AIassistance
  • Ensure AI-generated output meetsCluePoints’ engineering standards before submission

Spec-Driven Development

  • Work from approved specifications as thesingle sourceof truth
  • Collaborate with Product Managers and Tech Leads to refine technical scope
  • Implement features according to reviewed and approved specs
  • Maintain traceability between requirements, implementation, and tests

Architecture, Integration & Production Ownership

  • Handle complex integration points and system-level concerns
  • Address edge cases and performance considerations AI may miss
  • Contribute to architectural discussions and long-term technical decisions
  • Monitor productionbehaviorof AI-accelerated systems and proactively address stability, observability, and performance issues

Quality & Compliance

  • Review AI-generated code before raising pull requests
  • Increase andmaintaintest coverage through automated testing
  • Ensure outputs are secure, auditable, and aligned with regulatory expectations (GxPcontext)
  • Participate in code reviews and continuous improvement of engineering standards

Continuous Improvement

  • Experiment with new AI tools and workflows to increase productivity
  • Contribute to evolvingCluePoints’ AI-First engineering practices

Requirements

  • 5+ years of professional software engineering experience shipping production systems
  • Proficiencyin Python (essesntial) and/or TypeScript (experience with both is ideal)
  • Hands-on, daily use of AI coding assistants in real delivery workflows
  • Demonstrated ability to critically evaluate AI-generated code:identifyinghallucinations, security risks, architectural drift, and edge cases
  • Solid understanding of API design (REST), relational databases (MySQL or equivalent), and at least one NoSQL store
  • Strong testing discipline: unit, integration, and end-to-end testing as part of your normal workflow
  • Experience with Spec-Driven Development frameworks such asOpenSpec,SpecKit, BMAD, or Superpowers
  • Comfort working in a regulated or compliance-sensitive environment, or willingness to learnGxPexpectations quickly

Strong Advantage

  • Experience with Angular or a modern frontend framework
  • Experience building structured AI-assisted workflows (prompt pipelines, agent orchestration, automated review systems)
  • Microsoft Azure cloud experience
  • Background in life sciences, healthcare, or other regulated industries

Bonus

  • Contributions to open-source AI tooling or developer productivity projects
  • Experience with CI/CD pipeline design and DevOps practices
  • Familiarity with clinical trial data, CDISC standards, or RBQM concepts

Our Technology Stack

Note* You do not need deep experience in every part of this stack, but you should be comfortable working across backend and frontend and confident in ramping quickly on unfamiliar technologies — with AI as an accelerator, not a crutch.

Medical Virtual Assistant (MVA)

Remote | Chiropractic Clinic | 30 Hours/Week | $5-$6/hour
performance-based increase after 6 months

Position Overview

We are seeking a highly capable Medical Virtual Assistant (MVA) to support the overall operational health of a busy healthcare clinic. This role is ideal for someone who is very sharp, proactive, detail-oriented, emotionally intelligent, and able to take ownership of important clinic workflows with minimal supervision.

This is not a basic task-following role. The ideal candidate must be able to think ahead, identify operational gaps, take initiative, and help remove administrative and billing-related tasks from the provider's plate.

We are looking for someone with excellent English communication skills, strong executive presence, high accountability, and the ability to build a trust-based working relationship with the provider and care team.

Key Responsibilities

Insurance Verification

Verify patient insurance after the patient checks in, typically around 15 minutes after the scheduled appointment time. Ensure all insurance information is accurate, updated, and properly documented.

Denied Claims Management

Review denied claims, identify denial reasons, and assist with claim reprocessing. Track issues, follow up on missing information, and help prevent repeat claim errors.

EOB Processing

Review and process Explanation of Benefits documents. Help organize, validate, and clear EOB backlogs while ensuring billing and insurance documentation is accurate.

Patient Balance Resolution

Review outstanding insurance balances and patient account issues. Track unresolved balances, identify the source of the issue, and coordinate next steps for resolution.

Claims Processing

Support claims-related workflows, including Cigna and Veterans Affairs claims. Ensure claims are reviewed, tracked, and escalated when necessary.

Payment Coordination

Assist with vendor payment coordination, including check payments when needed. Ensure payment-related tasks are completed accurately and on time.

SOAP Note Monitoring

Monitor SOAP note completion, accuracy, and compliance. Track missing, incomplete, or delayed documentation and communicate concerns appropriately.

Appointment Tracking

Track missed appointments, canceled appointments, and scheduling trends. Identify patterns that may affect clinic revenue, patient flow, or provider productivity.

Reports and Operational Tracking

Prepare reports on outstanding balances, missed appointments, canceled appointments, EOB backlog, denied claims, and other operational metrics. Reports should include clear insights and practical recommendations when needed.

Team Coordination

Support smooth communication between the provider, care team, and administrative staff. Help ensure updates are clearly shared, priorities are followed through, and important tasks are not missed.

Operational Support

Proactively identify workflow gaps, billing concerns, documentation delays, scheduling issues, and patient account problems. Recommend practical solutions to improve clinic efficiency.

Mandatory Requirements

  • Minimum of 1 year of experience as a Medical Virtual Assistant

  • Experience supporting a US healthcare practice

  • Experience with insurance verification, EOBs, claims, denied claims, patient balances, or billing support

  • Exposure to CPT and ICD-10 codes

  • Strong English communication skills, both written and verbal

  • Strong executive presence and professional communication style

  • Must be a Mac OS user

  • Strong attention to detail and follow-through

  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision

  • Proven leadership, ownership, or high-accountability experience in a previous role

Required Soft Skills

  • Proactive and able to anticipate needs before being asked

  • Highly detail-oriented with billing, documentation, and reporting tasks

  • Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills

  • Emotionally intelligent and patient when working with a busy provider

  • Confident, professional, and organized in communication

  • Able to take personal responsibility for assigned work

  • Resourceful and self-motivated when learning new workflows

  • Trustworthy, dependable, and comfortable handling sensitive information

Nice to Have

  • Prior experience supporting a chiropractic clinic

  • Experience with Cigna or Veterans Affairs claims

  • Experience clearing EOB or billing backlogs

  • Experience preparing operational or billing reports

  • Experience mentoring, training, or supporting new team members

  • Experience working closely with a clinic owner, provider, or executive-level leader

Schedule and Compensation

  • Schedule: Monday to Friday

  • Hours: 6 hours per day, 30 hours per week

  • Rate: $6 per hour

  • Work Setup: Remote

  • Device Requirement: Mac OS required

Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is someone who does not wait to be told every step. This person should be observant, organized, and confident enough to identify what needs attention.

They should be able to manage detailed billing and administrative tasks while also thinking about the bigger picture of clinic operations. The right candidate will be sharp, emotionally intelligent, highly reliable, and capable of becoming a trusted operational support partner for the provider and care team.

raw.description:
The Project Manager is a client-facing role at the center of everything we do.
Running high-impact A/B tests requires coordination across many disciplines—research, strategy, design, copywriting, development, QA, analytics, and client stakeholders. Your job is to keep everything moving forward, aligned, and energized.

Key Responsibilities

You’ll own three core responsibilities:
  1. Coordination. You’ll manage cross-functional teams of 5–10 people and ensure tests move smoothly from idea → build → launch → analysis. You’ll spot risks early, unblock teams, and make sure nothing falls through the cracks.
  2. Strategy & Planning. You’ll help build and maintain a testing roadmap of 10–20 upcoming experiments. You’ll communicate the “why” behind the plan, set expectations, and walk clients through progress and results in weekly meetings.
  3. Energy (“Vibes”). You’re the main point of contact for clients and internal teams. You bring clarity, positivity, and momentum. When things get busy or complicated, you keep people focused and motivated.

Skills, Knowledge and Traits

You do not need prior A/B testing experience or even formal project management experience. We will train you. Here’s what we need from you:
  1. Organization and diligence. You like systems, checklists, and timelines. You front-load work, plan ahead, and don’t stop until things are finished properly.
  2. Communication. You default to over-communication. You proactively reach out to clients and teammates, flag risks early, and ask for help when you need it.
  3. Smart and high agency. You learn quickly, enjoy technology and design, and want to understand why things work (or don’t). You’re the kind of person who notices patterns and asks good questions.

What You’ll Get

  • Clear promotion opportunities. We invest heavily in training and promote almost exclusively from within. Most leaders at Spiralyze started in entry-level roles.
  • Indefinite contract. This role is offered as a permanent position, giving you the opportunity to grow and develop over the long term.
  • Tech reimbursement. Need a better computer, monitor, or setup? Want training on Figma or GA4? We’ll help.
  • In-demand skills. You’ll learn Conversion Rate Optimization from the most experienced experimentation teams in the world.
  • Time to recharge. 20 days of paid vacation plus holidays.
If you’re excited about working with smart people, solving real problems, and growing fast in a merit-based environment, we’d love to hear from you.

The regional accounting manager is one of several peer roles across the organization who support other clinical trials site locations in the overall Headlands Research network. Please note: This position is restricted to candidates based in LATAM. Candidates in other locations will not be considered for this role.

Key Responsibilities

  • Utilize your sound knowledge of Project Management Best Practices and the Agile/Scrum framework to help the team and client follow the process.

Skills, Knowledge, and Expertise

The ideal candidate will demonstrate:

  • Accountability, strong communication, facilitation and interpersonal skills, and technical aptitude.
  • Ability to develop and sustain a passion for the client’s vision with our internal team.
  • Strong ability to build relationships, communicate with, and present to a multitude of client stakeholders at various levels of organizations.
  • Experience as an IT Project and/or Program Manager, managing a team of developers and testers, and working with other client teams.
  • Experience in website and/or mobile application development, and custom software development activities and projects
  • Experience as a Scrum Master working with both IT and Business organizations.
  • Work independently without close supervision.

  • Preferred experience with application lifecycle management tools, such as JIRA.

ITX’s Compensation Philosophy

Equality in compensation has been our practice since ITX started in 1997.

ITX believes that market-based pay ensures fair and equitable compensation for our worldwide team members and pay that is based on the market, not on who has the best negotiation skills. At ITX, you’ll never discover that someone in the same job with the same experience makes more than you, or that there are pay gaps based on race, gender, disability, or age.

How do our team members experience market-based pay at ITX? We gather market data to benchmark each position in our candidates’ and team members’ locations and use these benchmarks for candidate offers and to perform regular compensation reviews for our team members. You’ll never have to worry about asking for a pay raise again. At least once a year ITX automatically adjusts pay when the benchmark is higher than our team member’s compensation.

Here's what one of our team members has to say about ITX’s compensation philosophy:

"I like how straightforward the Salary Review Process is – it’s very organized, it’s very conversational, and not intimidating. I like that is more focused on the fair market value of what and how we’re doing. Everything about this process works for me – it feels like a very smooth process from start to finish". Steven W. Scrum Master / Program Manager at ITX

In LATAM, the pay range for a Project Manager role is $4,500 to $6,300 monthly,depending on experience, specific skills and certifications, and education. Based on your location in LATAM, pay ranges could be adjusted according to local market data, which can vary from country to country. These variation percentages could be 15% lower or 27% higher.

Do you have questions about ITX’s compensation practices? Let us know! We’re proud of how we do compensation at ITX and welcome the opportunity to share more.

About Global Citizen

Global Citizen is the world’s leading international advocacy organisation on a mission to end extreme poverty NOW. Powered by a worldwide community of everyday activists raising their voices and taking action, the movement is amplified by campaigns and events that convene leaders in music, entertainment, public policy, media, philanthropy and the corporate sector. Over the past 10 years, $50 billion in commitments announced on Global Citizen platforms has been deployed, impacting 1.3 billion lives. Established in Australia in 2008, Global Citizen’s team operates from New York, Washington DC, Los Angeles, London, Paris, Berlin, Geneva, Melbourne, Toronto, Johannesburg, Lagos and beyond.

Role Overview: (Full-Time Continuous Employment)

Global Citizen’s PR & Communications department is seeking a dynamic PR professional with a passion for innovative storytelling, sharp news sense, and a strong contact list of industry-leading journalists across Europe, the Middle East and Africa to help further Global Citizen’s mission to end extreme poverty and drive positive impact globally.

Reporting to the VP of PR & Communications, the objective of the Director, Public Relations & Communications, EMEA, is to protect and promote Global Citizen’s brand in Europe, the Middle East and Africa. This is done through proactive and thoughtful sourcing and pitching of news from and for the organization, and building and maintaining a network of journalists and social influencers to which these stories can be shared with. The job requires tight management skills and the ability to nurture a team of outside press officers and agencies on a consistent basis. This is a full time, ongoing role responsible for leading Global Citizen’s PR activities in key markets, including but not limited to:

  • Europe: UK, France, Germany, Spain
  • Africa: South Africa, Rwanda, Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya
  • MENA: UAE

This role will also oversee the PR agencies working on Move Afrika, and is responsible for the development and execution of the Move Afrika PR plan. This role will also drive Global Citizen’s G7 and G20 media strategy and tactics.

The ideal candidate will have experience collaborating internationally with colleagues, partners and agencies to execute large-scale public relations campaigns. They will be a self-starter, with the flexibility to adapt quickly, sharp attention to detail, a positive, solution-oriented mindset, tight organization skills, and the confidence to work with counterparts and stakeholders across all professional levels.

This role will lead on outreach and maintaining relationships with journalists in the above key markets with tier-1 outlets and platforms, formulating innovative and timely pitches that elevate Global Citizen’s campaigns, events and executive spokespeople to new and existing audiences across sectors. The Director, Public Relations & Communications EMEA will develop and execute PR strategies for priority initiatives in close coordination with the New York office, including the Artist Relations, Marketing, Brand Partnerships and Global Policy & Advocacy departments, with support from external PR agencies in Africa and Abu Dhabi.

The ideal candidate will have a robust contact list of key reporters in verticals including music & entertainment, policy, philanthropy and/or business; outstanding writing and communication skills; confidence working across timezones, languages and cultures; experience working on large-scale live events; and knowledge of tools and platforms such as Muck Rack, Meltwater, and PR Newswire.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Media Relations (60%)
    • Foster and maintain strong relationships with key reporters at top tier media outlets, including entertainment, hard news and political outlets, both domestically and internationally.
    • Ideate, pitch and secure innovative stories to reach key and new audiences, with a focus on Global Citizen’s strategic objectives, vision and impact.
    • Identify and pursue interview and thought leadership opportunities for Global Citizen’s senior executives and spokespeople at key events, conferences and summits, and on podcasts.
  • PR Campaigns & Events (30%)
    • Lead the execution of PR campaigns related to Global Citizen’s campaigns, events, brand partnerships and special projects across EMEA.
    • Draft, proof and edit materials, including press releases, interview briefs, press statements, bios, backgrounders, etc.
    • Logistical coordination leading up to and during live events, press conferences, junkets, briefings, etc.
    • Oversee the day-to-day management of public relations agencies in EMEA driving strong alignment and positive results.
  • Team Administration (10%)
    • Liaise with all departments leading up to and during live events and tentpole campaigns in EMEA.
    • Schedule meetings and calls with internal and external groups across time zones, including scheduling media interviews and briefings for executives.
    • Maintain and organize the PR team drive and archives for designated markets, events and projects.

Required Competencies:

Education & Experience

  • A Bachelor’s or Master's degree or equivalent, ideally in Public Relations, Corporate Communications, Journalism or Marketing
  • 5-8 years experience running global campaigns in entertainment, media or politics

Attributes

  • Strong media relationships across top tier hard news, entertainment and/or political media outlets, in key markets described above
  • Strong understanding of the global news landscape and the evolving digital media landscape, with a particular focus on social-first new media
  • Excellent communication skills, with demonstrated ability to write varied high level materials and present complex topics clearly and succinctly
  • Capacity to understand and analyze complex information and turn it into accessible messaging and make thoughtful recommendations
  • Experience executing press events and/or activations; confidence liaising with members of the press and high profile individuals
  • Strong news sense and analytical skills, ability to anticipate and mitigate potential problems,
  • A nimble approach to complex tasks, with the flexibility to adapt quickly; diligent, organized, with excellent attention to detail in a fast-paced environment with competing priorities
  • Team player with a hunger to achieve excellent results; resourceful and proactive with a positive attitude and inclusive style that energizes and mobilizes the team
  • Confidentiality, discretion and trustworthiness a must
  • Additional language skills desired
  • Using AI tools to work smarter and drive impact is an essential part of every role at Global Citizen. All staff must integrate AI into their daily work, whether improving workflows, analyzing information, or enhancing communication in service of our mission.
  • Passionate about global development and engaging audiences with Global Citizen’s mission and brand. Maintain a commitment to eradicating extreme poverty in our lifetime

Benefits

Why Global Citizen?

In this coming decade of action and accountability, Global Citizen will be the leading international voice, educator, and influencer that rallies humanity to take full responsibility and accountability for eradicating extreme poverty. You have a chance to contribute and make this world a better place for all.

More Details

  • Must be authorized for employment in the UK or the EU
  • This role is fully remote
  • Compensation: £66,000 Annual Salary (£5,500/month)

raw.title: US Audience Growth Consultant
raw.excerpt: 350. org is seeking a senior consultant on Audience Growth on Social Media to deliver content production targeting US audiences within our global social media channels, with a focus on measurable audience growth across our shared global platforms.
raw.description:
350.org is seeking a senior consultant on Audience Growth on Social Media to deliver content production targeting US audiences within our global social media channels, with a focus on measurable audience growth across our shared global platforms. This is a temporary, results-oriented assignment.

The consultant is a senior professional with demonstrated expertise across the full social media lifecycle: strategic planning, performance evaluation, and content production – as well as hands-on experience setting up and optimizing awareness and growth advertising campaigns.

The Global Communications Director is the contract manager and is responsible for approving deliverables and authorizing invoices. The Consultant will participate in agreed fortnightly progress reviews.

  • Commitment: The assignment is estimated at approximately 100 full-time consultant days during the period of 6 months, invoiced monthly against deliverable progress.
  • Location: Remote within the United States, preferably in EST timezone.
  • Hourly rate: $49.15

Scope of Work

Deliverables:

  • An audience growth plan and its execution for 350.org's global social media channels (Instagram and Facebook) among US-based audiences, aligned with the KPI targets outlined below.
  • A dedicated growth project for the 350 Action US Instagram account, aimed at reaching the 10,000-follower target outlined below.
  • At least one message-testing project focused on energy affordability, connected to and informing the Great Power Shift campaign.
  • A final set of recommendations, delivered by the end of the contract, covering: priority audience segments, key messages to prioritize going forward, and practices to continue, based on data and insights gathered throughout the assignment.

Key Performance Indicators:

  • Growth of 20% in the US-based following of 350.org's global Instagram and Facebook pages, especially within the age segment of 25 - 45 years old.
  • Growth of the 350 Action US account to 10,000 followers.
  • Increased engagement rate (likes, comments, shares, saves, video views, click-through rate on Linktree and petition links) among US-focused posts on global pages.
  • Improved conversion rate on calls-to-action (e.g., petition sign-ups, sign-ups via Linktree) attributable to US-targeted content and advertising.
  • Benchmarking will be conducted at the start of the assignment.

Main Duties include:

Strategy and Content Localization:

  • Develop and execute a US-audience social media growth strategy aligned with global campaign priorities and organizational KPIs.
  • Adapt global campaign narratives, key messages, and creative assets for US audiences, calibrating tone, cultural framing, and format while maintaining brand consistency with the organization's global voice.
  • Produce at least 15 content pieces per month across all channels, including short-form video, copy, and visual content optimized for US audiences, applying platform-specific best practices (aspect ratios, captioning, hook structure, posting cadence, content trends) for distribution across the organization's global Instagram and Facebook channels, as well as the 350 Action US account.
  • Develop a content review protocol, with criteria and workflow for assessing incoming global content for risk of underperformance or cultural misalignment with US audiences. Apply the protocol to review each piece of content as it comes in (approximately 5 pieces per week), providing feedback within 24 hours of submission.
  • Coordinate with global communications colleagues on audience segmentation, content production, and publishing schedules. Apply geolocation and audience segmentation protocols when publishing US-specific content, to preserve relevance for non-US followers on shared global channels.
  • Liaise with Digital Engagement and Global Social Media colleagues to localize and adapt CTAs for the US audience context.

Audience Insight and Evaluation:

  • Analyze engagement and growth metrics for US-based followers (including reach, impressions, engagement rate, follower growth rate, and audience retention) using platform analytics and social listening tools. Submit findings and recommendations to the Global Social Media team.
  • Deliver proactive and timely content strategy recommendations and outputs, based on ongoing monitoring of US cultural discourse, platform algorithm updates, creative trends, and emerging social/media narratives.
  • Design and interpret A/B and message testing protocols targeted at US audiences, using statistically sound sample sizes and control variables.
  • Track performance against growth KPIs and iterate tactics based on data analysis.

Advertising:

  • Set up, manage, and evaluate paid awareness and growth advertising campaigns (e.g. Meta Ads) to support follower growth objectives.
  • Optimize ad targeting parameters, budget allocation, bidding strategy, and creative assets based on performance metrics including CPM, CPC, CTR, conversion rate, and ROAS (return on ad spend).
  • Monitor cost-efficiency indicators (CPA, cost-per-follower) and advise budget allocation across campaigns/ad sets to maximize return on investment, with approval from the Global Communications Director.

Crisis Communication:

  • Support the global communications team in developing and executing crisis communication protocols relevant to US audiences and platforms.
  • Monitor for reputational risk indicators or fast-moving situations requiring rapid-response content.

Qualifications and Experience:

Required:

  • Senior-level experience in social media strategy, with a demonstrated track record of driving measurable audience growth.
  • Tech-savvy, with proven experience adapting content and strategy to platform algorithm changes and evolving creative trends, leveraging these shifts to drive performance improvements.
  • Hands-on experience creating and publishing content for Instagram and Facebook, including copy, graphics, and short-form video production. Proficiency with Canva.
  • Experience setting up, managing, and evaluating paid social advertising campaigns, with fluency in core performance metrics (CPM, CTR, CPA, ROAS, conversion rate).
  • Proficiency with audience insight and social listening tools (e.g. Google Trends/Insights, Junkipedia, Brandwatch or similar) to inform content and strategic decisions.
  • Proven senior experience in crisis communication and rapid response situations.
  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to translate performance data into actionable strategy and concrete content outputs.
  • Strong writing skills in English, with demonstrated ability to adapt tone and voice across audience segments.

Desirable:

  • Experience with advocacy, campaigning, or nonprofit communications.
  • Spanish as a secondary language.

raw.title: Senior Director of Audience & Community (Contract)
raw.excerpt: Remote with Required On-Site Presence in Los Angeles (April 4th - 6th, 2026)Bully Pulpit International is an outcomes agency made up of strategists, data scientists, and artists.
raw.description:
Remote with Required On-Site Presence in Los Angeles (April 4th - 6th, 2026)

Bully Pulpit International is an outcomes agency made up of strategists, data scientists, and artists. We come from politics, brands, and government and we communicate without barriers and measure what matters. We have more than 400 team members in six countries and thirteen offices — Berlin, Brussels, Chicago, D.C., London, Los Angeles, New York, Oslo, San Francisco, and Zürich. We apply our unique expertise across strategic communications, public affairs, research, and digital marketing to create sophisticated and customized strategies that make change possible for both American and European clients.

About the Convening:

A Day of Unreasonable Conversation (UC) is an invitation-only annual summit which serves as a

trusted, curated space designed to foster honest, nuanced, and critical discourse on the most urgent

issues of our time. The gathering bridges the gap between the entertainment industry and social

impact sectors. It connects "culture shapers"—influential television writers, showrunners, producers,

executives, and digital storytellers who are literally writing the script for the world—with frontline

changemakers, advocates, philanthropists, and issue experts.

The core mission of UC is to "unlock progress through the power of stories". In a deeply polarized

moment where trust in traditional media is at a record low, the event aims to spark writers' rooms with

new ideas and give creators the tools to drive meaningful change. UC challenges storytellers to

complicate the narrative by moving beyond flat tropes and oversimplified binaries to explore the

systemic complexities of our time. Ultimately, the goal is to bring greater nuance, empathy, and truth to

the stories that shape public perception.

UC is grounded in the belief that culture is the multiplier for change at scale. Because culture sits

upstream of policy and politics, it is where people already are. Even in times of deep fracture when

people stop listening to experts or political parties, they still listen to stories. By bringing storytellers and

problem-solvers together, UC seeks to turn stage-side insights into long-term creative collaborations

that shift culture on screen and beyond.

A Day of Unreasonable Conversation is founded and produced by the social impact agency Propper

Daley x Bully Pulpit International (BPI). The event relies on cross-sector collaboration and is fully funded

by philanthropy.

Requirements

We’re hiring a Senior Director of Audience & Community, reporting directly to the Executive Director, to build and steward the community at the heart of A Day of Unreasonable Conversation. This person will own the full audience function—from strategy and curation through CRM, outreach, guest experience, day-of execution, and long-term relationship building. We’re looking for someone who sees the audience as a strategic asset and a living network, not a static guest list, and who can build and run this function with real authority and minimal oversight.

While the Day of Unreasonable Conversation is the community's annual gathering, this role is also responsible for activating that community throughout the year through small convenings (Evenings of Unreasonable Conversations), fellowships, editorial touchpoints, and ongoing relationship stewardship that keeps people connected between convenings.

Curation matters as much as headcount. We want a room with genuine diversity across perspectives, creative backgrounds, and positions in the industry. That means thinking carefully about what each person’s pr

What You’ll Do

Strategy & Curation

  • Own the audience composition strategy. Curate a room of approximately 500 guests that brings together the entertainment industry and the social impact sector. The audience should reflect both the trusted relationships UC has built over time and the creators, executives, organizations, and changemakers whose work is most relevant to the cultural conversation in the year of the convening. Every year’s room should feel intentional, current, and additive.
    • Lead the audience strategy for three Evenings of Unreasonable Conversations, curating intimate gatherings that introduce new voices, deepen relationships within the existing community, and intentionally funnel participants into the annual Day of Unreasonable Conversation.
  • Entertainment side: Writers and showrunners, producers and directors, network and studio executives who greenlight content, digital creators and online storytellers reflecting how culture is created and distributed today, and industry gatekeepers including agents, managers, and publicists—who shape which stories and talent reach audiences.
  • Social impact side: Frontline activists, researchers, policy experts, nonprofit and foundation leaders, and people with lived experience who bring subject-matter expertise and real-world perspective into the room.
  • Own audience strategy beyond “filling the room.” Build a year-round community, not a one-day guest list. Define the audience function as a pipeline into fellowships, future convenings, and ongoing engagement, with clear goals for room composition, ideological and sector diversity, cultural influence, and long-term relationship building.
  • Build and maintain the ecosystem map. Create and steward a living map of aligned organizations (studios, networks, production companies, nonprofits, advocacy groups, foundations, agencies, etc.), maintaining relationships throughout the year so UC is continuously expanding and strengthening its community rather than rebuilding it each event cycle.
  • Develop audience engagement strategies for different community segments, including returning attendees, fellows, funders, creative leaders, first-time participants, and strategic partners, ensuring each group has meaningful opportunities to engage with UC throughout the year.
  • Run a tiered outreach and room-design strategy. Execute a Tier 1/2/3 invitation rollout against defined room-mix targets by sector, geography, ideology, influence, and creative discipline. Identify hub connectors at major studios, agencies, platforms, and organizations to help recruit attendees, and track progress against those targets throughout the invitation period, not just at the finish line.

Systems & Reporting

  • Own the CRM and audience database as a strategic system. Move the function off ad hoc tools and onto an integrated platform that supports registration, segmentation, and year-round relationship tracking, and tag attendees by role, influence, funder relationship, fellowship potential, dietary restrictions, and special needs so the data serves more than one event cycle.
  • Design a multi-stakeholder reporting structure. Build dashboards and metrics that translate raw audience data into clear, digestible insights for the Executive Director, funders, and cross-functional teams, so different stakeholders can see exactly what they need without you rebuilding the reporting each time.
  • Maintain live tracking and report progress on a set cadence. Keep a single master tracker covering RSVP health, room mix, VIP allocation, and flake rates, and report against goals in a weekly check-in with the Executive Director and cross-functional partners (Talent, Editorial, Fellowships, Fundraising) so the room is built deliberately over time, not assembled in a last-minute push.
  • Serve as the senior owner of cross-functional audience alignment. Define how the Audience & Community function interfaces with Talent, Editorial, Fundraising, Fellowships, and Production so audience decisions are explicitly tied to broader program goals, operating within clear guardrails and decision rights rather than relying on constant escalation.
  • Define and track outcome KPIs, not just operational metrics. Set targets for guest satisfaction, repeat engagement, and year-over-year retention, and report progress against them alongside room mix and RSVP data.
  • Track year-round community health. You are measuring participation across Evenings, fellowships, editorial engagement, repeat attendance, introductions made, and other indicators of long-term relationship growth—not just annual event attendance.
  • Run structured, proactive workflows. Build and manage the outreach calendar, invitation workflows, and templates for each audience segment, including the review and approval timeline across key stakeholders so materials move through sign-off without stalling, and independently hit deadlines and turnaround times without needing to be chased or have work taken over.
  • Own the working relationship with the graphic designer for audience-facing communications. Brief the designer directly on invitations, templates, and outreach materials, manage revisions and turnaround, and bring finished assets to the Executive Director for approval rather than routing every step through her.

Guest Experience & Day-of Operations

  • Bridge audience development and the day-of guest experience. Design the full guest journey from first invitation through on-site arrival, seating, and departure, working directly with production and logistics so the invitation process and hospitality experience feel like one seamless continuum rather than separate tracks.
  • Develop the audience logistics packet and manage partner fulfillment. Ensure funders, speakers, co-chairs, and key partners have their guests properly accommodated, from invitations and registration through on-site hospitality and special requests.
  • Own day-of audience operations. Lead registration and check-in protocols, VIP and priority guest handling, real-time seating and room-fill management, and serve as the final decision maker on live audience issues throughout the event.

Post-Event & Cross-Functional Leadership

  • Lead post-event learning and long-term relationship building. Manage the distribution and analysis of post-event audience surveys, capture structured feedback and impact data, report key insights to leadership and funders, and build a thoughtful, tiered follow-up strategy that connects attendees to fellowships, Evenings, future convenings, and other opportunities for continued engagement.
  • Develop and execute a year-round audience engagement calendar: that includes editorial updates, digital briefings, community check-ins, and opportunities for members to contribute to UC research, storytelling, fellowships, and future programming.
  • Build and steward a curated network of "UC Friendlies": trusted writers, creators, executives, researchers, philanthropists, and cultural leaders who can be activated throughout the year as contributors, moderators, hosts, advisors, speakers, fellowship participants, or connectors into new communities.

What You Bring

  • 8–10+ years in audience development, community strategy, membership, partnerships, or relationship-driven leadership roles in media, entertainment, philanthropy, or live experiences, with a demonstrated track record of building and stewarding communities and networks over time.
  • Demonstrated success building and activating communities over time—not simply managing audiences for individual events with the ability to turn participants into long-term collaborators, contributors, and ambassadors.
  • Senior enough to hold real decision-making authority across both audience development (strategy, curation, invitations) and audience management (hospitality, guest experience), managing them as one cohesive function rather than two disconnected tracks.
  • Deep knowledge of the entertainment and social-impact ecosystem, with genuine relationships across television, film, digital media, agencies, studios, philanthropy, nonprofits, advocacy organizations, and other culture-shaping communities.
  • Excellent judgment and creative instincts for audience curation. You know how to preserve trusted relationships while continually bringing new voices into the community, finding unconventional paths to the right room instead of relying on the same invite list every year.
  • Experience integrating relationship management with hospitality operations, including VIP travel, guest communications, registration, seating, and on-site experience, so every interaction feels like part of one cohesive guest journey.
  • Hands-on experience building and owning a CRM or audience platform (such as Whova, Cvent, Swapcard, or Swoogo) as a year-round relationship management system, not simply an event registration tool.
  • Comfortable directing and briefing creative execution. You can brief a designer clearly, give useful feedback on drafts, and bring polished, on-brand materials forward for final approval rather than requiring hands-on creative direction from leadership at every step.
  • Exceptional systems thinker with strong project management instincts. You naturally build scalable workflows, trackers, reporting structures, and operating systems that make teams more effective.
  • Rigorous attention to detail and reporting discipline. You build and maintain accurate, structured tracking and reporting systems as a matter of habit, not an afterthought.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently and proactively. You hit deadlines, manage your own communications cadence, and drive work forward without needing to be pushed or having projects taken over.
  • Comfortable owning ambiguity and defining scope. You can build a new function and establish its guardrails rather than waiting for detailed direction.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills for funder-facing reporting, VIP correspondence, and cross-functional collaboration.
  • Able to work in an intensive event environment. The weeks leading into the convening require significant focus and availability, and major personal travel should be planned outside this period.
  • Must be able to be on-site in Los Angeles for event pre-production and the convening (April 4–6).

Customers, including Anthropic, Bloomberg, NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Salesforce, rely on Grafana Labs. We are a 100% remote company with team members across 40+ countries, backed by leading investors including Lightspeed Venture Partners, Sequoia Capital, GIC, Coatue, J.P. Morgan, CapitalG, and Lead Edge Capital. Learn more at and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

We’re scaling fast and staying true to what makes us different: an open-source legacy, a global collaborative culture, and a passion for meaningful work. Our team thrives in an innovation-driven environment where transparency, autonomy, and trust fuel everything we do.

You may not meet every requirement, and that’s okay. If this role excites you, we’d love you to raise your hand for what could be a truly career-defining opportunity.

This is a remote position. We are looking for candidates in the US and Canada.

The Opportunity:

As our Cloud / Grafana-as-a-service business continues to grow, we've started to change Grafana's core architecture to be fully multi-tenant and scalable, as well as a solid platform for our opinionated Cloud apps.

We're looking for someone with a lot of experience with SaaS platforms at scale. We are turning Grafana into a proper observability app platform where OSS and proprietary apps can directly tap into dashboards, alerts, incidents, and telemetry and deliver even more integrated experiences.

To get there, we need to refactor a big part of Grafana so that it’s simpler and standardized. Grafana is used by countless OSS and Cloud users across different platforms, so planning and rolling out changes safely to avoid service disruptions is crucial; we are looking for someone who is excited about this sort of work.

What You’ll Be Doing:

  • Coding new features, enhancing the operational experience of the systems you develop, and iteratively improving them based on production insights
  • Authoring, contributing to and reviewing design documents
  • Taking an active role in shaping the roadmap
  • Mentoring and supporting other team members and collaborating with different teams across the organization
  • Owning the experience of our customers by participating in weekday 12h x 5d and a separate weekend 24h x 2d on-call rotations.

We invest heavily in developer productivity. You can use modern AI coding assistants as part of your daily workflow (your choice of tools, within security guidelines), backed by a company-funded usage budget so you can iterate quickly without unnecessary friction.

We encourage pragmatic AI-assisted development: faster prototyping, test generation, refactors, documentation, and incident follow-ups—always paired with strong code review and quality standards.

  • You are pragmatic; you prioritize progress over perfection; you can handle ambiguity.
  • We are using Golang on the backend; you are either already familiar with Golang or are excited to learn the language

In Canada, the compensation range for this role is $186,368 - $223,642 CAD. Actual compensation may vary based on level, experience, and skillset as assessed throughout the interview process. NTT DATA strives to hire exceptional, innovative and passionate individuals who want to grow with us. If you want to be part of an inclusive, adaptable, and forward-thinking organization, apply now.

We are currently seeking a Data Senior Engineer - Data Modernization & Archiving - Remote to join our team in Toronto, Ontario (CA-ON), Canada (CA).

Senior Developer – Data Modernization & Archiving

Project Overview

We are seeking Senior Developers to support a data modernization and archiving initiative involving the migration of historical financial data from a legacy UNISYS mainframe environment to a secure, scalable, and user-friendly archival solution.

The successful candidates will bring strong experience in Microsoft Power BI, Oracle PL/SQL, and ETL development, with a proven ability to work across data analysis, data modelling, migration, business intelligence, reporting, validation, testing, integration, and deployment.

Working closely with business and technical stakeholders, the Senior Developers will help design and implement solutions that meet requirements for data quality, reporting, performance, governance, and long-term data retention.

Key Responsibilities

  • Gather, analyze, validate, and translate business and technical requirements into functional and technical specifications.
  • Analyze legacy and source-system data and develop data models, mappings, business rules, and data structures.
  • Design, develop, and maintain Oracle PL/SQL and ETL processes supporting data migration, transformation, and archival.
  • Design, develop, and enhance Microsoft Power BI dashboards, reports, datasets, and visualizations.
  • Develop business intelligence and ad-hoc reporting solutions to support business and operational requirements.
  • Integrate reporting and data solutions with existing applications, databases, and other data sources.
  • Develop data validation, reconciliation, error-handling, and quality assurance processes to ensure data integrity.
  • Perform unit testing, data validation, troubleshooting, performance tuning, and defect resolution.

  • Support solution deployment, production implementation, release activities, and post-deployment support.
  • Provide user training, knowledge transfer, and transition-to-support activities.

Required Qualifications

  • 5+ years of experience working as a Senior Software Developer, Senior Programmer, or in a comparable senior technical role.
  • 5+ years of experience with data analysis, data modelling, data mapping, and integration of multiple data sources.
  • 2+ years of hands-on experience with Oracle PL/SQL and ETL development.
  • 2+ years of experience developing business intelligence reports, dashboards, datasets, and data visualizations using Microsoft Power BI.
  • 2+ years of experience designing or implementing data migration and/or archival solutions, including data validation, reconciliation, quality assurance, testing, and troubleshooting.

About Enertiv

Enertiv is a leading proptech SaaS platform that integrates hardware-enabled data collection with AI-powered analytics to transform how commercial real estate portfolios are operated. Our technology enables owners and operators to reduce operating costs, improve sustainability, and deliver enhanced tenant experiences.

We’re at a pivotal moment in our growth. To scale effectively, we need stronger operational foundations, clearer accountability, and disciplined execution. This role is designed for a senior operations leader with a strong engineering mindset who can build the systems, standards, and operating rhythms required for our next phase.

Client Success Manager

Reports to: Manager, Client Success

Location: Full time, US Remote (Colorado candidates preferred), minimal travel.

Compensation: $85,000-$105,000 base + potential performance bonus + equity

The Role

To support our continued growth, Enertiv is seeking an experienced Client Success Manager to build strategic client relationships, drive platform adoption, and help clients realize measurable business value. This individual will manage a portfolio of high-value clients, partnering closely with the Account Management (AM) team to drive retention and account growth while serving as the primary owner of customer health, adoption, value realization, and long-term success. This position reports directly to the Manager of Client Success and can be based remotely within the U.S.

This role represents a unique opportunity to join a fast-moving, mission-driven team that's helping modernize and decarbonize the real estate industry.

What You’ll Own

  • Partner with the Onboarding team throughout kickoff and implementation to ensure a strong foundation, accelerate time-to-value, and lead cross-functional resolution of client delivery and support issues across maintenance, data, software, and ESG workflows.
  • Own customer health by monitoring health signals, maintaining accurate account data, and proactively mitigating risk before issues impact retention.
  • Lead Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) focused on adoption, platform health, and value realization, while partnering with AM team on Executive Business Reviews (EBRs) centered on strategic outcomes and long-term business value.
  • Partner with the Asset Performance Services (APS) team to deliver client insights, measurement and verification (M&V) reporting, and proof-of-value deliverables that reinforce customer outcomes.
  • Partner with the AM team to identify expansion opportunities, support renewal planning, and advance long-term account growth through proactive forecasting and strategic account planning.
  • Act as the voice of the customer by surfacing client feedback and market insights to Product and Leadership to influence roadmap priorities and service improvements.

What Success Looks Like

First 90 Days:

  • Build a strong foundation: Complete Enertiv platform and industry onboarding, establish relationships with key client stakeholders, and confidently articulate Enertiv's value proposition.
  • Successfully transition your portfolio: Deliver or schedule initial QBRs for priority accounts while maintaining accurate CRM data, customer health scores, and renewal forecasts.

Ongoing:

  • Drive customer value and adoption: Deliver impactful QBRs, increase platform engagement, and achieve 60%+ multi-product adoption by aligning Enertiv's solutions to customer business objectives.
  • Build trusted client partnerships: Develop relationships with two or more key stakeholders per account, serving as a strategic advisor to Asset Management, Sustainability/ESG, and Property Management leaders.
  • Support retention and account growth: Partner with the AM team to proactively mitigate risk, maintain 120%+ net revenue retention and 95%+ gross revenue retention, and advance upsell, cross-sell, and expansion opportunities contributing to $500K+ in annual net new ARR.
  • Demonstrate strategic impact: Consistently reinforce business value, strengthen executive alignment, and help customers achieve measurable operational and sustainability outcomes.

Qualifications & Skills

Required:

  • 3+ years of client success experience in B2B SaaS managing a portfolio of customers and driving retention, renewals, and account growth.
  • Experience managing complex, multi-stakeholder customer relationships.
  • Highly organized and data-driven, with experience using customer health metrics, CRM systems, and business insights to prioritize work and manage a portfolio effectively.

Preferred:

  • Experience in PropTech, commercial real estate technology, or real estate operations, with familiarity working with building owners, property managers, or asset managers.
  • Familiarity with energy management, utility data, sustainability reporting (LL97, GRESB, ENERGY STAR Portfolio Manager, etc.), or adjacent sustainability technologies.
  • Experience with Zoho CRM and Notion.

Location

Full time, US Remote (Colorado candidates preferred), minimal travel.

Compensation

$85,000 to $105,000 with potential performance bonus and equity.

We offer a competitive total rewards package designed to support your health, growth, and flexibility. Employees can choose from multiple medical plan options (HSA and PPO), plus dental and vision coverage, company-paid life insurance, and access to a 401(k). Eligible team members participate in performance-based bonuses and equity opportunities. We provide a company laptop and home office stipend, flexible PTO, 10 paid holidays, paid parental leave, and hybrid/remote flexibility. You’ll also benefit from monthly Lunch & Learns, professional development support, and a $2,000 referral bonus for successful hires.

raw.description:
Location: Remote

Reports to: Global Program Manager

Duration: 6 months

Time Commitment: This is a project-based position with defined deliverables; time commitment per week during the 6 month duration may vary.

Organization Overview

The Elba Hope Foundation is a nonprofit organization. At our heart lies a steadfast commitment to sustainable progress and better futures for Africans and the African Diaspora through the interconnected tools of agriculture, conservation, food security, education, youth advocacy, and social justice. Our mission is to drive transformative change by fostering innovation, empowering communities, and forming strategic partnerships that will have a lasting impact on these sectors, both today and for future generations.

Position Overview

The Elba Hope Foundation is seeking a Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) Advisor to strengthen the organization’s approach to program monitoring, performance measurement, learning, and reporting across programs in the United Kingdom (UK), Sierra Leone (SL), and the United States (US). The Advisor will develop a practical, harmonized MEAL framework that supports consistent measurement across the organization while allowing for appropriate adaptation to each country and program context. A core focus of the assignment will be to establish the plans, tools, workflows, and systems required for continued monitoring beyond the consultancy period.

Key Responsibilities

The Advisor will work with relevant program and leadership teams to:

  • Develop MEAL plans and frameworks for each program.
  • Define appropriate indicators, data sources, collection methods, responsibilities, and reporting schedules.
  • Develop standardized and context-specific monitoring and data collection tools.
  • Establish workflows and systems for routine collection, validation, analysis, reporting, and use of program data.
  • Strengthen organizational capacity to maintain and use the MEAL system on an ongoing basis.
  • Support staff training, documentation, and handover to ensure sustainability after the consultancy ends.

Qualifications

The preferred consultant should demonstrate:

  • Significant professional experience in monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning.
  • Experience designing organizational or multi-program MEAL systems.
  • Demonstrated experience developing MEAL plans, indicators, data collection tools, and reporting frameworks.
  • Experience building monitoring workflows and sustainable data management processes.
  • Strong understanding of quantitative and qualitative monitoring methods.
  • Experience supporting programs operating across multiple countries or contexts.
  • Ability to translate technical MEAL concepts into practical tools for program staff.
  • Experience delivering staff training and capacity building.
  • Strong analytical, facilitation, and technical writing skills.

Experience working with global programs, or comparable contexts is desirable.

Deliverables

The consultancy will result in a practical, proportionate, and sustainable MEAL system that EHF staff can operate and maintain using existing organizational capacity and Google Workspace.

The Advisor will develop one common EHF MEAL architecture, with program-specific adaptations where required for Hope Power Project, Creative Futures, and DYSF. The Advisor is expected to build on existing systems and materials wherever practical rather than recreate tools or processes that are already fit for purpose.The total fixed professional fee for satisfactory completion of the scope is USD$28,000, payable upon EHF's acceptance of the following deliverables:

  1. Contract Execution & Approved Workplan: Finalized contract; kickoff meeting; agreed methodology, workplan, consultation schedule, and document/data request.
  2. MEAL Diagnostic & Implementation Priorities: Focused assessment of existing MEAL practices, tools, data, partner reporting, prior research, and staff capacity across the three programs; identification of gaps and assets that can be retained; prioritized recommendations for system development.
  3. EHF Organizational MEAL Framework & Master Indicator Framework: One common EHF results and measurement architecture; manageable organizational and program indicator set; indicator definitions, data sources, collection frequencies, responsibilities, quality standards, reporting expectations, and approach to learning and adaptation.
  4. Program MEAL Plans: Operational measurement plans/matrices focused on Hope Power Project, with lighter engagements for Creative Futures and DYSF. Creative Futures includes practical longer-term tracking of skills, confidence, and employment outcomes; DYSF includes media, awareness, advocacy, event, and public/policy engagement measures; Hope Power receives the greatest technical depth across electricity, digital access/skills, education/employment, livelihoods/economic outcomes, and agricultural training.
  5. MEAL Toolkit & Accountability Tools: Standardized data-collection and reporting templates; partner reporting tools; participant feedback and outcome tools; longitudinal follow-up tools where appropriate; data-quality checks; learning/reflection templates; and necessary Hope Power-specific tools. Includes a formal, proportionate Hope Power community feedback and complaints-response mechanism.
  6. EHF Data Workflow & MEAL SOPs: Practical organization-wide workflow covering data collection/receipt, partner submission, validation, entry, storage, review, reporting, escalation, learning, and use. Concise MEAL SOP documenting roles, responsibilities, procedures, quality controls, and system maintenance.
  7. Google Sheets Performance Tracking System & Dashboard: Operational Google Sheets-based single source of truth for approved EHF program metrics; standardized data structures; program and organizational views; targets and actuals where appropriate; automated summaries/charts; validation controls; and instructions for routine updating and maintenance. EHF will prepare requested historical data for import.
  8. Staff Training & System Launch: Practical training for EHF staff who will enter, validate, manage, or use MEAL data to confirm that staff understand indicators, tools, workflow, quality requirements, dashboard use, accountability processes, and routine system maintenance.
  9. Live Pilot, Refinement & Final Handover: Support for one live reporting and data-collection cycle; assessment of usability, data quality, indicator clarity, workflow, and dashboard performance; reasonable refinements based on pilot findings; complete final package of approved materials; implementation / maintenance roadmap; final handover meeting.

Scope Parameters

The USD $28,000 fixed fee assumes a proportionate system designed for EHF's current organizational scale and operating model.

The scope assumes:

  • Three core programs: Hope Power Project, Creative Futures, and DSYF with the majority of the Advisor’s focus on the more complex Hope Power Project.
  • Creative Futures UK and emerging US delivery will use one common program MEAL approach, with limited geographic adaptations made by program staff where genuinely necessary.
  • Google Sheets will be the primary performance-tracking technology.
  • EHF will prepare historical data for migration in an agreed format.
  • The Advisor will design data-collection and assessment methodologies but will not conduct large-scale primary research, baseline studies, or impact evaluations.
  • The Advisor will support one live system pilot/reporting cycle.
  • The system will be designed for semiannual organizational performance review while allowing program data to be updated at appropriate intervals.

Benefits

  • Flexible remote work environment.
  • Opportunity to support sustainable and accountable M&E for a growing global nonprofit.
  • Collaborative, mission-driven team with meaningful international impact.

Application Instructions

Please submit your resume and a brief cover letter describing your experience and fit for the role. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled.

We are seeking candidates who bring a deep contextual understanding of Africa and a strong alignment with our mission and values. This may come through lived experience, long-term professional engagement, or meaningful personal connection to the regions and communities we serve. Our work is rooted in respect for local leadership, cultural knowledge, and community-driven solutions, and we prioritize applicants who demonstrate humility, accountability, and a clear commitment to working in partnership with diverse stakeholders.

The Elba Hope Foundation is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, national origin, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected characteristic.

Salary: USD $28,000 flat fee

Sumitomo Pharma Co., Ltd., is a global pharmaceutical company based in Japan with operations in the U.S. (Sumitomo Pharma America, Inc.), focused on addressing patient needs in oncology, urology, women's health, rare diseases, cell & gene therapies and CNS. With several marketed products and a diverse pipeline of early- to late-stage investigational assets, we aim to accelerate discovery, research, and development to bring novel therapies to patients sooner. For more information on SMPA, visit our website or follow us on LinkedIn.

Job Overview:

Director, Process Chemistry provides senior process chemistry expertise and technical leadership across development-stage small molecule programs, with the ability to evaluate, shape, and influence process chemistry decisions in a collaborative, matrixed environment reporting to the VP, CMC Development. The Director plays in active role in developing robust, scalable, and phase-appropriate drug substance manufacturing approaches from early development through commercialization, including route scouting, process optimization, impurity control strategy, scale-up, technology transfer, and external manufacturing oversight. This position works closely with internal and external partners across Analytical Development, Formulation Development, Supply Chain, Quality, Regulatory, and project teams to support timely progression of programs, reliable clinical and commercial supply, and successful regulatory submissions. This is a highly cross-functional role requiring strong scientific judgment, operational leadership, and the ability to influence decisions through expertise, collaboration, and trusted partnership across a matrixed global organization.


Essential Functions Required for Job:

  • Demonstrate leadership ability to shape drug substance development strategies for small molecule programs, bringing process chemistry expertise to support sound, aligned decisions across CMC, program, and corporate objectives.
  • Provide scientific and technical leadership on route selection, process development, optimization, control strategy, and scale-up, influencing clinical and commercial manufacturing decisions through data-driven recommendations and expert judgment.
  • Support oversight of external process development and manufacturing activities at CDMOs by providing technical input, risk identification, issue-resolution recommendations, and guidance on timelines, budgets, and deliverable quality.
  • Contribute to phase-appropriate control strategies for starting materials, intermediates, APIs, impurities, and critical process parameters in collaboration with Analytical Development, Quality, and other cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Provide technical input to technology transfer activities to manufacturing sites and support engineering, registration, validation, and commercial readiness activities as applicable.
  • Operate as a drug substance subject matter expert for regulatory submissions and agency interactions, including providing technical input and reviewing relevant sections of INDs, IMPDs, CTDs, NDAs MAAs, and responses to health authority questions.
  • Partner closely with cross-functional teams including Formulation Development, Analytical Development, Supply Chain, QA, Regulatory Affairs, and clinical teams to ensure integrated CMC execution and uninterrupted supply.
  • Facilitate scientific problem solving related to process performance, manufacturability, impurity trends, robustness, and lifecycle improvements by providing data-driven recommendations and influencing alignment.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with external partners, consultants, and contract laboratories to advance development objectives effectively and efficiently.
  • Mentor, coach, and develop scientists or matrix team members, while fostering a culture of scientific excellence, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
  • Contribute to portfolio strategy, due diligence, and business development assessments as needed.
  • Ensure accurate, timely, and inspection-ready documentation of development work, technical reports, and governance updates.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities (general & technical):

  • Strong leadership presence with the ability to influence direction, contribute to key technical decisions, provide sound scientific judgment, and support execution across complex, cross-functional programs.
  • Deep scientific curiosity and problem-solving capability, with a practical and risk-based approach to development challenges.
  • Excellent communication skills, including the ability to clearly present complex technical information to senior leadership and non-technical stakeholders.
  • High degree of organizational awareness and the ability to connect interdependencies across CMC functions and broader program objectives.
  • Strong collaboration and influencing skills, with success working in matrixed, global environments and with internal and external partners.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, adapt to changing business needs, and maintain focus on quality, timelines, and outcomes.
  • Commitment to developing talent, building effective teams, and fostering an inclusive and accountable work environment.
  • High degree of organizational awareness, ability to connect the dots to understand all the interdependency and big picture.

Education & Experience Requirements:

  • PhD in Organic Chemistry, Process Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Chemistry, or a related scientific discipline required; exceptional candidates with a Master’s or Bachelor’s degree and significant relevant industry experience may be considered.
  • A minimum of 10 years of relevant pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry experience in process chemistry or drug substance development, including meaningful experience providing technical leadership in cross-functional or matrixed settings.
  • Demonstrated expertise in synthetic route design, process optimization, scale-up, impurity control, and technology transfer for small molecule APIs.
  • Strong working knowledge of cGMP manufacturing, CMC development, regulatory expectations, and global quality standards relevant to drug substance development.
  • Experience authoring or reviewing regulatory submission content and supporting health authority interactions for drug substance sections.
  • Proven success working with external partners such as CDMOs and contract laboratories to provide technical oversight, identify risks, and influence high-quality outcomes on time and within budget.
  • Experience working in cross-functional teams supporting programs from early development through late-stage development and/or commercialization.
  • Prior people management experience is preferred, though strong matrix leadership experience will also be considered.
  • Ability to travel periodically as needed for CDMO visits, technical oversight, and internal meetings.
  • Ability to work effectively in a global, matrixed organization, including collaboration with international colleagues, external partners, and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Japanese language proficiency is a plus and would enhance collaboration and technical communication with Japanese colleagues engaged in global CMC development strategy and execution.
